relations: A draw-off from tank1 drives the h1 loop (pump 2) until it saturates and tank3 overfills; shifting production setpoint from tank1 to tank2 relieves it.
A pump-1 gain loss or a gamma1 decrease pushes pump-1 voltage toward saturation and drops h2; trading h2 setpoint down and h1 up restores production.
A sustained h3 near the limit signals excessive v2 from the tank1 loop, so shifting production to tank2 (lower h1 setpoint) relieves it.
A sustained h4 near the limit signals excessive v1 from the tank2 loop, so shifting production to tank1 (higher h1 setpoint) relieves it.
A tank1 draw-off raises v2 until it saturates at 12 V, letting h3 overfill; lowering the h1 setpoint shifts production to tank2 and restores h3 margin.
Regressing each tank's level-slope-plus-outflow against its feeding pump voltage returns the exact per-volt gain, separating split-valve shift from pump gain loss.
